title: AIPAC-Aligned Groups Gift Doris Matsui a $785k Blitz of Last-Minute Attack Ads
author: Julian Andreone
content:

AIPAC and aligned groups are funding a surge in last-minute spending behind
incumbent California Rep. Doris Matsui in an attempt to save the 82-year-old
Democrat from being unseated by her progressive challenger Mai Vang.

AIPAC itself is funneling the money through Pro-Choice Majority Action. Pro-
Choice Majority Action does not publicly associate with AIPAC, but it is
[legally affiliated directly](https://docquery.fec.gov/cgi-
bin/forms/C00949248/1972138/) with EDW Action, which has been established by
Drop Site and others as a known AIPAC passthrough PAC. EDW Action has used
Pro-Choice Majority in elections across the country, including the hotly
contested primary to succeed Nancy Pelosi in San Francisco and against Melat
Kiros before her landmark victory against 30-year incumbent Rep. Diana DeGette
in Denver.

The [Pro-Choice Majority
ad](https://adstransparency.google.com/advertiser/AR17694564123288797185/creative/CR00380428317381099521?region=US&topic=political)
against Mai Vang says the Sacramento city councilwoman is "all for herself"
and accuses her of missing 40% of regional transit board meetings, saying,
"When she showed up, she slashed public funds for affordable housing and
homelessness"--a confusing accusation given Vang's record. The Sacramento
Regional Transit Board itself [formally commended](https://www.sacrt.com/wp-
content/uploads/board-documents/archived-board-
documents/2025/SacRT%20Board%20of%20Directors%20-%20%20January%2027,%202025%20-%20%20Combined%20File.pdf)
Vang in January 2025. Vang has also voted to [redirect city resources
allocated for the police department to its homelessness
response](https://sacramento.newsreview.com/news/sacramento-city-council-oks-
budget-rejects-proposal-to-move-police-funding-to-homeless-services-7aa92a75)
efforts, and she has [proposed](https://statehornet.com/2026/10/mai-vang-
doris-matsui-congress-california-politics-election-democrats-republicans-
socialismi-dont-have-the-luxury-of-waiting-mai-vang-envisions-a-government-
for-working-people/) both a $200 billion national affordable housing trust
fund and expansion of the Low-Income Housing Tax Credit, which incentivizes
private investors to subsidize the construction of affordable housing across
the country.

The practice of using passthroughs to obscure its support has become common as
AIPAC grapples with how toxic its pro-Israel bribery has turned with voters.
This week, AIPAC announced it was ending endorsements and direct contributions
to candidates after the midterms, opting to use its super PAC United Democracy
Project and obfuscating passthrough PACs instead.

Pro-Choice Majority [reserved](https://docquery.fec.gov/cgi-
bin/fecimg/?202610159908916465) $300,000 of negative ads against Vang on
October 5, comprising roughly 40% of the total $785,000 being spent on
Matsui's behalf in the home stretch.

The remaining $485,000 is [coming from Affordable
California](https://docquery.fec.gov/pdf/263/202610089908583263/202610089908583263.pdf),
which lists a Dallas address and one donor. The American Foundation for Good
Government
[dumped](https://docquery.fec.gov/pdf/926/202610079908567926/202610079908567926.pdf)
$500,000 into it on October 7. The PAC reserved its ads against Vang that same
day. The American Foundation for Good Government, established in March, is a
501(c)(4), which means its donors do not need to be disclosed. Notably, it
spent in Michigan this cycle, helping to bankroll Michigan Forward 2026, which
in turn donated to A Stronger Michigan. Both organizations were key spenders
among a network of AIPAC-aligned PACs that bled more than $17 million
attacking Abdul El-Sayed and boosting Haley Stevens in the state's Democratic
Senate primary.

[Affordable California's
ad](https://kpipolitical.com/alerts/db8586a0-0de5-42b3-97ac-542c850c9869) hits
Vang for earning support from Hasan Piker and the Democratic Socialists of
America. It also includes a clip of Vang facing away from the American flag as
the pledge of allegiance is recited while her peers on the city council face
toward it. Elsewhere in California, in another Democrat-against-Democrat
general election that features a strong critic of Israel, Jimmy Gomez is
similarly urging super PACs to run ads on Piker.

Neither Matsui nor her campaign could be reached for comment. An AIPAC
spokesperson pointed to a [public
statement](https://x.com/aipac/status/2114338633117221104?s=46) the
organization released regarding Matsui spending, saying, "Despite conspiracy
theories, not every dollar spent to defeat extremist candidates comes from
AIPAC."

Matsui's position on Israel and Gaza has evolved to some extent since AIPAC
included her on its list of endorsees in 2024. The congresswoman has begun
referring to Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu as a "war criminal" and
said she opposes sending "offensive dollars" to Israel. Matsui has not signed
on as a co-sponsor to the Block the Bombs Act, the most basic legislative
vehicle to restricting the transfer of these "offensive dollars," a
distinction without any functional meaning given that money is fungible, to
Israel's Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich. She declines to call Israel's
actions a "genocide" and backs a two-state solution.

Aside from the large sum of money Matsui's campaign has received from AIPAC-
aligned special interest groups, the congresswoman has also loaned herself a
total of $6.9 million, most recently in installments of $2.59 million and
$1.52 million on
[Friday](https://x.com/catargetbot0001/status/2113465759754293474?s=46) and
[Sunday](https://x.com/rpyers/status/2114480879108288625), respectively.

Vang defeated Matsui in the June primary election by a margin of 31.2% to
29.2%, but because California has a "jungle primary" the top two vote
receivers advance to the general election irrespective of party affiliation.
Zacharia Wooden, the Republican candidate in the primary who came in third
place, received 45,994 votes. The [only available public polling in the
race](https://x.com/daveweigel/status/2094893722127192118?s=20), conducted by
Data for Progress in mid-August, shows Vang widening her lead from 2 points to
4, boasting a 32% to 28% lead with 40% of voters either undecided or planning
to sit out.
